key_insight: A physics-guided conditional diffusion model can synthesize realistic rare-event water-gas shift trajectories, enabling better fault diagnosis when abnormal process data are scarce.
engineering_relevance: This approach helps improve hydrogen-production process safety and reliability by augmenting rare abnormal-condition data for monitoring and early warning.
method: Conditioned diffusion model generates rare-event process trajectories beyond the normal training regime.
Physics guidance embeds reaction governing laws to keep synthetic profiles physically consistent.
Augmented data are used to train diagnosis models and a hazard score ranks operating-risk severity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that simulations show the physics-guided diffusion model produces higher-quality synthetic data and better rare-event diagnosis than data-driven baselines.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the embedded physics assumptions and how well the model generalizes to unseen operating conditions.
paper_title: Physics-Guided Conditional Diffusion Model for Rare Event Synthesis and Diagnosis for the Water-Gas Shift Reaction
